text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: High anomalous auth traffic to /v1/auth from unusual IPs; possible log upload flagged by DLP rule. Priority: P1. Details in thread, please ack.

sre-oncall: acked. I'm on it, switching to incident channel. Who's onsec? @eng-security?

eng-security: I'm here. Quick summary pls.

sre-oncall: We saw a surge of 401->200 followed by large PUTs to our internal log-archiver S3 bucket from a staging worker pool. Rate ~120/min over 8m. IDS DLP flagged potential PII in payload.

dmitri: pasting sample from the log-forwarder logs:
```
2026-10-04T12:23:11Z forwarder-7f8c PUT s3://internal-archive/2026/10/04/ctx_9a8b.gz size=12MB status=200 src=10.142.88.23 user=svc-logging-prod token=svc-abc123...
2026-10-04T12:23:13Z auth-proxy-2 GET /v1/auth?key=svc-abc123 src=10.142.88.23 result=200
```
Noticing same svc token used for staging worker and archive uploads.

maria.ops: any customer impact observed? Are production tokens affected?

dmitri: initial look shows token belongs to a staging service account (svc-logging-staging). No direct prod token seen yet but logs include paths referencing project IDs that overlap with prod indexes (likely mixed env logs).

raj.sinha: rotate the staging service account key immediately and revoke sessions tied to that token. I'll prep rotation steps.

michelle: agreed, but we need containment first: block egress from the offending host range and suspend write perms for internal-archive bucket while we investigate. Who can run the bucket policy change now?

sre-oncall: I'm applying a temporary deny on PutObject to internal-archive for principals matching svc-logging-staging.* and adding a bucket-lock entry. Will also push a security-group rule to block 10.142.88.0/24 egress to external hosts.

eng-security: good. Also start a quick grep across recent uploads for filenames containing user identifiers. Use the search query: `ctx_*` and filter by size>1MB between 2026-10-04T11:00 and 2026-10-04T13:00.

dmitri: running search now. Preliminary: ~38 files matching, downloading first 5 for review.

elena.cs: if any PII confirmed, we need a customer-impact list and timeline for notifications. What's our tentative timeline for findings?

maria.ops: also, any chance this is a misconfigured staging exporter that pointed at internal-archive by accident? That would be configuration error not malicious, but still sensitive.

dmitri: initial evidence looks like misconfigured exporter combined with a leaked staging token. No sign of external exfil to non-aws endpoints yet; uploads are to our S3. But DLP found strings matching email and partial phone patterns in some gz payloads.

raj.sinha: rotation plan: 1) revoke svc-logging-staging key 2) issue new key with least privileges 3) force restart of staging exporters with new key 4) run token revocation script to invalidate sessions. I can run steps 1-3 in next 10m.

michelle: I'll own comms. Drafting internal incident page and will prepare a customer notification template in case PII confirmed. Tagging legal now. @eng-security assume root cause triage after containment.

eng-security: tagging legal and compliance. Also capture all relevant audit logs, S3 access logs, and KMS usage before we rotate keys (so we can correlate). We should snapshot the bucket and store a read-only copy in a secure quarantine bucket for forensics.

sre-oncall: snapshotting internal-archive to quarantine-internal-352987, setting lifecycle to retain for 90d, read-only. Pausing further automated archival jobs to avoid more writes.

dmitri: confirmed 5 files with high-confidence email addresses in payload. Saving hashes and moving to quarantine. Will redact copies for analysts.

elena.cs: ok, assume PII confirmed. Michelle, legal, what's our notification cadence? We need to decide if we do customer-by-customer or aggregate notice.

michelle: counsel says prepare for targeted notification to affected customers and a proactive post for the status page. We'll wait for full list (should be <10 customers likely). Target: initial reach-out within 3 hours.

raj.sinha: rotation done for svc-logging-staging. New key deployed, old key revoked. Pushed new policy to deny s3:PutObject from revoked principals.

sre-oncall: egress block applied for 10.142.88.0/24, bucket writes paused. Snapshot copied and quarantine set.

dmitri: continuing scan, will attach list of affected resources and sample redacted payloads to the incident doc.

eng-security: next steps: full root-cause (config drift vs credential leak), review IAM permissions for all staging/service accounts, and ensure separation of staging/prod buckets via tagging and org-level policy.

michelle: thanks team. I'll update the incident ticket with current mitigation and comms plan. If anything changes escalate to execs.

sre-oncall: handing off to second shift @sre-oncall-2 for monitoring; I'll drop runbook notes in the incident doc.

sre-oncall-2: ack. Monitoring alerts in place, will watch for suspicious retries or other hosts.

incident-bot: Incident recorded: 3529876543. Status: Mitigation in progress. Assigned: eng-security, sre-oncall-2, legal, cs.

michelle: closing loop for now; keep thread updated with any new customer-impact findings. :lock:
